from django.db.models import Prefetch
from django.test import TestCase
from .models import Author, Book, Bookmark, TaggedItem


class T(TestCase):
    def test_all(self):
        b1 = Book.objects.create(title="b1")
        b2 = Book.objects.create(title="b2")
        authors = [Author.objects.create(name=f"a{i}", first_book=b1 if i < 3 else b2) for i in range(6)]
        b1.authors.set(authors[:4])
        b2.authors.set(authors[2:])
        with self.assertNumQueries(2):
            books = list(Book.objects.prefetch_related(Prefetch(
                "first_time_authors", Author.objects.order_by("-name")[1:3], to_attr="x")))
        self.assertEqual([a.name for a in books[0].x], ["a1", "a0"])
        self.assertEqual([a.name for a in books[1].x], ["a4", "a3"])
        books = list(Book.objects.prefetch_related(Prefetch("authors", Author.objects.all()[:2], to_attr="x")))
        self.assertEqual([a.name for a in books[0].x], ["a0", "a1"])
        self.assertEqual([a.name for a in books[1].x], ["a2", "a3"])
        books = list(Book.objects.prefetch_related(Prefetch("authors", Author.objects.order_by("-name")[1:])))
        self.assertEqual([a.name for a in books[0].authors.all()], ["a2", "a1", "a0"])
        authors = list(Author.objects.prefetch_related(Prefetch("books", Book.objects.order_by("-title")[:1], to_attr="x")))
        self.assertEqual([[b.title for b in a.x] for a in authors], [["b1"], ["b1"], ["b2"], ["b2"], ["b2"], ["b2"]])
        bm1 = Bookmark.objects.create(url="http://a")
        bm2 = Bookmark.objects.create(url="http://b")
        for bm in (bm1, bm2):
            for t in "abc":
                TaggedItem.objects.create(tag=t, content_object=bm)
        bms = list(Bookmark.objects.prefetch_related(Prefetch("tags", TaggedItem.objects.order_by("-tag")[:2], to_attr="x")))
        self.assertEqual([[t.tag for t in b.x] for b in bms], [["c", "b"], ["c", "b"]])

content.text:
`Prefetch()` now accepts sliced querysets, so the example from the issue works. Each category gets its own `[:3]`, not three posts in total. I checked this with a throwaway test that I've since deleted: reverse foreign key, many-to-many and generic relations all came back correct. That included offset slices like `[1:3]` and `[1:]`, plus custom ordering. The 988 tests across prefetch, relation, queries, window-function and multi-database suites pass, with 15 skipped and 2 expected failures. I didn't add a permanent test, so the hidden tests will be the only lasting check.

**How it works:** the slice is taken off the query and redone per related object in SQL. Each row is numbered within its group using `ROW_NUMBER()`, a window function, and only rows inside the slice bounds are kept. This relies on the window-function filtering added in the previous commit. For many-to-many I checked the generated SQL: it still joins the link table once.

**Changes:**
- `django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py`: a new helper that applies the per-object slice. It's used in two places:
  - when fetching prefetched rows for reverse foreign keys and many-to-many;
  - in `_apply_rel_filters`, which runs when the prefetched results are stored on each object. Without this, the "Cannot filter a query once a slice has been taken" error still happened there.
- `django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py`: the same handling for generic relations, grouped by content type and object id.
- `docs/releases/4.2.txt`: a release note.

**Limitation:** on databases without window functions, prefetching with a sliced queryset raises `NotSupportedError`, which says the database needs window-function support.

Forward foreign key and one-to-one prefetches are unchanged, since slicing there means little.
